# Task: resolve issue #6933 — determine whether anything consumes shared ~/.grok mtimes for liveness; fix scope or close with evidence

## Evidence rules (#M-4)
The verdict (consumes vs not) must be backed by the actual code paths quoted — trace every reader of ~/.grok (and any GROK_* liveness env/paths) across the watchdog, adapters, monitors, and delegate runner. An AST/grep sweep alone is not proof for "nothing consumes" — check indirection (config-derived paths).

## Steps
1. Read issue #6933. Trace all consumers of the shared ~/.grok directory (or grok liveness signals generally) in the runtime/watchdog/monitoring stack.
2. If NOTHING consumes it for liveness: post the traced evidence as the closing comment yourself is not possible — return the evidence note as your result; the driver closes. No PR.
3. If something DOES consume it: scope that signal per-session (session-specific artifact), add a two-session guard test (mutation-checked: reverting to the shared path makes the test fail), PR (Fixes #6933). No scope creep beyond the liveness signal.
4. Work in your dispatch worktree if (and only if) a code fix is warranted; investigation may run read-only from the worktree either way.
5. Do NOT arm auto-merge and do NOT merge.
